mainTopic: The privileges of a תלמיד חכם, including freedom from the head tax; רב אשי's sale of wood to a fire temple; and a new משנה on vows timed by the harvest and the rains.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a list of honors that a תלמיד חכם shares with a כהן: reading first, blessing first, and choosing a portion first. רבא then rules that a תלמיד חכם may refuse to pay the head tax. He bases this on a פסוק in עזרא that freed the Temple workers from royal taxes, and רבי יהודה explains its three tax words. רבא adds that a scholar may even say 'I am a servant of fire' to escape the tax, because he is only chasing a lion away from himself. Next comes a story: רב אשי sold his forest to a fire temple. רבינא challenges him with לפני עור, and רב אשי answers that most wood is used for heating. A new משנה then explains vows tied to seasons: 'until the harvest' means the wheat harvest, timed by the place of the vow. 'Until the rains' is the second rainfall, and 'until the rains stop' is the end of ניסן or after פסח. The גמרא brings a ברייתא showing that a vow follows the place where it was made, even after the person travels. It ends with רבי זירא limiting the rain dispute to someone who said 'rains' in the plural.

steps.title: Finishing the list of honors: going first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא completes a list of privileges: to open first, to bless first, and to take a nice portion first.
steps.simpleTranslation: To open first, to bless first, and to take a nice portion first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a list that started before this section. The list names honors given to a כהן, and here they are applied to a תלמיד חכם too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list names three ways of going first: opening, meaning reading first from the תורה; saying the blessing first; and choosing the best share first when portions are handed out. The earlier part of the discussion taught that a תלמיד חכם gets these same honors.

keyTerms.meaning: to open, meaning to be called first to read from the תורה
to say the blessing, such as leading ברכת המזון

steps.whyThisMatters: It sets up the idea behind the whole section: a תלמיד חכם is treated with the special status of a כהן. רבא builds on this idea next.

phrases.english: To open first,
phrases.notes: This means being called up first to read from the תורה.

phrases.english: and to bless first,
and to take a nice portion first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a list from the part of the daf that comes just before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן, and so also a תלמיד חכם, gets to read first, bless first, and choose a portion first.

steps.title: A Torah scholar may refuse to pay the head tax
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that a תלמיד חכם may say 'I will not pay the head tax,' and brings a פסוק from עזרא as his source.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: A Torah scholar is allowed to say, 'I will not pay the head tax,' because it is written: 'It shall not be lawful to impose מנדה, בלו, and הלך upon them.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא teaches a new rule: a תלמיד חכם may refuse to pay the head tax. He backs it up with a פסוק about the Temple workers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In עזרא, the Persian king freed the כהנים, the לוים and the other Temple workers from his taxes. Since a תלמיד חכם has the status of a כהן, as the discussion just before this taught, he gets this freedom from tax too.

keyTerms.meaning: the head tax, a tax charged on each person

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that being treated like a כהן also brings practical benefits, not only honor.

phrases.english: Rava said:
It is permitted for a Torah scholar to say:
I will not pay the head tax,
as it is written: 'Minda, belo and halakh,
it shall not be lawful to impose upon them.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: שְׁרֵי לֵיהּ לְצוּרְבָּא מֵרַבָּנַן לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the idea that a תלמיד חכם is like a כהן and applies it to taxes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A תלמיד חכם may refuse to pay the head tax.

steps.title: Explaining the three tax words in the verse
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה explains the three words in the פסוק: מנדה is the king's portion, בלו is the head tax, and הלך is ארנונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: 'מנדה' is the king's portion. 'בלו' is the head-tax money. 'הלך' is ארנונא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבי יהודה to explain what each tax word in the פסוק means. His explanation shows that the head tax is one of the taxes the פסוק names.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This connects the פסוק to רבא's ruling. 'בלו' is the head tax, so the פסוק directly frees the Temple workers from it, and the תלמיד חכם shares that freedom.

keyTerms.meaning: the king's portion, a royal tax
head money, the tax charged on each person
ארנונא, a levy on people and their animals for work in the king's service

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda said:
'Minda': this is the king's portion,
'Belo': this is the head-tax money,
'And halakh': this is arnona.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: מִנְדָּה זוֹ מְנָת הַמֶּלֶךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the words of the פסוק that רבא quoted, showing that the head tax is included.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'בלו' in the פסוק refers to the head tax, so the exemption covers it.
steps.whatToRemember: A תלמיד חכם is like a כהן, so he is free from the royal taxes the פסוק names, including the head tax ('בלו').

steps.title: A scholar may say he is a servant of fire
steps.stepSummary: רבא adds that a תלמיד חכם may say 'I am a servant of fire, I will not pay the head tax.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: A Torah scholar is allowed to say, 'I am a servant of fire; I will not pay the head tax.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second, more surprising rule. A scholar may say 'I am a servant of fire' so the fire-worshipping government will free him from the tax.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In that time and place, the servants of the fire religion did not pay the head tax. The statement sounds like he is claiming to belong to an idol cult, which is why the גמרא will next ask how this can be allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: a servant of fire, meaning someone who serves in the fire-worship religion

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not allowing a person to actually serve idols. It is only a statement made to avoid the tax, and many explain that he can really mean a servant of ה׳, whom the תורה calls a 'consuming fire.'

phrases.english: And Rava said:
It is permitted for a Torah scholar to say:
'I am a servant of fire,'
phrases.notes: The fire-worship priests of that time did not pay the head tax.

phrases.english: 'I will not pay the head tax.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבָא: שְׁרֵי לֵיהּ לְצוּרְבָּא מֵרַבָּנַן לְמֵימַר עַבְדָּא דְנוּרָא אֲנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second teaching of רבא on the same topic, going even further than the first.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A תלמיד חכם may say 'I am a servant of fire' to avoid the head tax.

steps.title: Why is this statement allowed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason that such a statement is allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why a scholar may say something that sounds like belonging to idol worship. This question sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying you serve another religion sounds forbidden, so the ruling needs a reason. The question is a real request for the logic behind the ruling, not an attack on it.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind רבא's second ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a scholar may make a statement that sounds like serving idols.

steps.title: He is only chasing away a lion
steps.stepSummary: The answer: he says it only to chase a lion away from himself, meaning to protect himself from harm.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is saying it to chase a lion away from himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the scholar is only protecting himself. The unfair tax is like a lion attacking him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words are not a real statement of belief. They are a way to get out of danger or loss, the way a person would scare off a lion. Because the purpose is self-protection, the words are allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: to chase away, to make something run off

phrases.english: He is saying it to chase a lion away from himself.
phrases.notes: The 'lion' is a picture for the tax collector, or the loss he would suffer.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He says it only to protect himself from harm, not as a real statement of belief.
steps.whatToRemember: A scholar may say 'I am a servant of fire' to escape the tax, because he is only protecting himself, like scaring off a lion.

steps.title: רב אשי sells his forest to a fire temple
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tells that רב אשי had a forest and sold it to the house of fire.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי had a certain forest. He sold it to the house of fire.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story about fire-worshippers. רב אשי sold the wood of his forest to their temple, and this sets up רבינא's challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fire temple used wood to keep its fires burning, and some of those fires were part of their worship. That raises a question: did רב אשי help them worship idols?

keyTerms.meaning: the house of fire, the fire-worship temple

phrases.aramaic: רַב אָשֵׁי הֲוָה לֵיהּ הָהוּא אִבָּא,
phrases.english: Rav Ashi had a certain forest,
he sold it to the house of fire.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי הֲוָה לֵיהּ הָהוּא אִבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story linked to the earlier topic of fire-worshippers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב אשי sold the wood of his forest to a fire temple.

steps.title: רבינא objects: what about לפני עור?
steps.stepSummary: רבינא challenges רב אשי with the איסור of לפני עור לא תתן מכשול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: But there is the rule 'Do not put a stumbling block before the blind'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא challenges רב אשי's sale. He argues that it breaks the איסור of helping others sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: לפני עור also forbids helping someone do an עבירה. If the wood is used to worship fire, selling it means helping idol worship.

keyTerms.meaning: do not put a stumbling block before the blind, which also forbids helping someone sin

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:
But there is: 'Before the blind,
do not put a stumbling block!'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי: הָאִיכָּא לִפְנֵי עִוֵּר לֹא תִתֵּן מִכְשׁוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the sale described in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's sale of wood to the fire temple.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The wood may be used for idol worship, so selling it is helping someone sin, which לפני עור forbids.

steps.title: Most wood is just for heating
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that most wood is used for heating, so there is no problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Most wood is given for heating.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי defends the sale. He explains that most wood bought by the temple is burned for ordinary heating, not for worship.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since most of the wood goes to ordinary use, we follow the majority and do not assume his wood will be used for idol worship. So there is no לפני עור.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Most wood is given for heating.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: רוֹב עֵצִים לְהַסָּקָה נִיתְּנוּ
steps.terutzResolutionType: Following the majority: most wood is not used for idol worship.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Selling wood to a fire temple helps idol worship and breaks לפני עור.
steps.terutzMaskana: Most wood is burned for heating, so the sale does not count as helping idol worship.
steps.whatToRemember: רב אשי was allowed to sell wood to the fire temple because most wood is used for heating, so there is no לפני עור.

steps.title: A vow until the harvest means the wheat harvest in the place of the vow
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a vow 'until the harvest' lasts until the wheat harvest begins, and the timing follows the place where the vow was made.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone vows 'until the harvest', the vow lasts until people start harvesting wheat, not barley. The timing depends on where he made the vow: on a mountain, we follow the mountain's harvest; in a valley, we follow the valley's harvest.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It explains what 'until the harvest' means in a נדר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two harvests, barley and later wheat. The משנה says the person meant the main harvest, wheat. Since harvest comes at different times in different places, we go by the place where he made the vow.

keyTerms.meaning: The barley harvest, which comes earlier
The place where he made his vow

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule 'everything follows the place of the vow' is the basis for the ברייתא the גמרא brings in step 13.

phrases.english: MISHNA: "Until the harvest"

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁיַּתְחִיל הֶעָם לִקְצוֹר קְצִיר חִטִּין,
phrases.english: means until the people begin to reap the wheat harvest
but not the barley harvest.
Everything follows the place of his vow.
If he was on a mountain, then the mountain;
phrases.notes: He means we go by the harvest time on the mountain.

phrases.english: and if he was in a valley, then the valley.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the story of רב אשי and his forest ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Until the harvest' means until the wheat harvest begins, timed by the place where the vow was made.

steps.title: A vow until the rains: the actual second rainfall or its expected time
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא says a vow 'until the rains' lasts until the second rainfall actually falls. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says it lasts only until the time of that rainfall arrives.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone vows 'until the rains' or 'until there will be rains', the vow lasts until the second rainfall comes down. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: until the time for that rainfall arrives.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to vows tied to the rains and records a מחלוקת about when such a vow ends.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion waits for real rain to fall. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says the person meant the rainy season's date, so the vow ends on that date even if no rain has fallen.

keyTerms.meaning: The second rainfall of the rainy season

steps.confusionAlert: Both opinions agree the vow is about the second rainfall. They only disagree on whether rain must actually fall or whether its date is enough.

phrases.english: "Until the rains," or "until there will be the rains"
means until the second rainfall comes down.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
Until the time of the rainfall arrives.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with another seasonal time-limit, this time rain.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תנא קמא: until the second rainfall actually falls. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: until its expected time.

steps.title: A vow until the rains stop: end of ניסן or after פסח
steps.stepSummary: For a vow 'until the rains stop', רבי מאיר says it lasts until all of ניסן is over, and רבי יהודה says until פסח has passed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone vows 'until the rains stop', the vow lasts until the whole month of ניסן is over. These are the words of רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה says: until פסח has passed.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes with the opposite case: a vow that lasts until the rainy season ends. Again there is a מחלוקת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions set a fixed date for the end of the rains. רבי מאיר sets it at the end of ניסן. רבי יהודה sets an earlier date, right after פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: These are the words of רבי מאיר

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה gives three rules: 'harvest' means wheat harvest, timed by the place. 'Rains' means the second rainfall, with a מחלוקת over actual rain versus its date. 'Rains stop' means the end of ניסן according to רבי מאיר, or after פסח according to רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: "Until the rains stop"
means until the whole of Nisan has gone out;
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: עַד שֶׁיַּעֲבוֹר הַפֶּסַח.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: Until Passover has passed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from a vow until the rains begin to a vow until the rains end.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: until the end of ניסן. רבי יהודה: until after פסח.

steps.title: A vow made in the גליל follows the גליל's summer, even in the valleys
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that someone who vowed 'until the summer' in the גליל stays bound until summer arrives in the גליל, even if he moved to the valleys where summer came earlier.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: Someone who vowed 'until the summer' in the גליל and then went down to the valleys stays forbidden, even though summer already arrived in the valleys. He must wait until summer arrives in the גליל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and brings a ברייתא that applies the משנה's rule, 'everything follows the place of the vow', to a person who travels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said the timing follows the place of the vow. The ברייתא adds a new detail: this is true even after the person moves somewhere else. Where he is now does not matter; only where he made the vow counts.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: GEMARA: It was taught in a baraita:
One who vows "until the summer" in the Galilee,
and then went down to the valleys,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהִגִּיעַ הַקַּיִץ בָּעֲמָקִים —
phrases.english: even though summer has arrived in the valleys,
he is forbidden until summer arrives in the Galilee.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands the משנה's rule 'הכל לפי מקום נדרו' from step 10 to a person who travels after making the vow.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vow's timing follows the place where it was made, even after the person has moved elsewhere.

steps.title: רבי זירא limits the rain dispute to someone who said 'rains' in the plural
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about 'until the rains'. רבי זירא says the מחלוקת applies only when the person said 'rains'. If he said 'rain', everyone agrees he meant the rainy season's date.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'Until the rains' or 'until there will be rains' means until the second rainfall comes down, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל disagrees. רבי זירא said: They only argue when he said 'until the rains'. But if he said 'until the rain', he means until the time of the rains.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the rain section of the משנה again so it can bring רבי זירא's comment on it. רבי זירא narrows the מחלוקת to a specific wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'rains' in the plural could mean real rainfall, so the תנאים argue. Saying 'rain' in the singular points to the rainy season as a time of year, so everyone agrees the vow ends on the date, even if no rain has fallen.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who comments on the משנה
The time of the rains, the rainy season

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two words: in this משנה, 'הגשמים' (rains, plural) is the wording they argue about, and 'הגשם' (rain, singular) is the wording everyone agrees means only the date.
steps.whatToRemember: The wording of a vow matters. 'Rain' in the singular means the rainy season's date according to everyone. Only 'rains' in the plural is under dispute.

phrases.english: "Until the rains," or "until there will be rains"
means until the second rainfall comes down;

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says, etc.
phrases.notes: 'Etc.' means the גמרא is pointing you back to the rest of the משנה from step 11.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
The dispute is where he said "until the rains";
but if he said "until the rain,"
he is saying until the time of the rains.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: מַחֲלוֹקֶת דְּאָמַר ״עַד הַגְּשָׁמִים״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the rain section of the משנה (step 11) after the ברייתא about the place of the vow.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מחלוקת applies only to 'עד הגשמים'. For 'עד הגשם', everyone agrees the vow lasts until the time of the rains.
